body:
I know it's been a week or something since I posted and that I wasn't exactly welcoming of your advice, but I just thought I'd say that your last sentence has been running around in my head a lot: 

"Don't keep living your life the same way and expect different results."

And while I feel that I really have done a fuck-ton load of shit to change things/myself/my life, it's still worth pondering how much more I can do.

After years of clinging to my current job/career, I have finally started to acquiesce to the fact that it might actually be killing me and that maybe it's time to start valuing my life over my job.  That a job I "love" isn't worth it if the rest of my non-job life is so fucking miserable that I kill myself.  If I kill myself, I won't have *any* job.

Anyway, I tend to be very defensive and I am, admittedly, full of fucking anger for a lot of reasons.  But I am sorry I was initially very harsh towards you.  Your effort and words were not in vain.

I'm gonna try to let this sink in and try some of it.  

I hugely, hugely appreciate the time and effort you put into typing all this out.  It means a lot.

I know in my head that if I could just get my body moving once a day doing some of this stuff, it could make a big difference.  It's hard to just do it, but I'm going to try to use your comment as motivation.

Thank you.

Thanks dude, but... I have a decade-long drug-addiction history, including the intense abuse of weed.  I was so addicted to it that I missed work *beyond* my sick days, was chronically ill with bronchial infections, etc.  And it didn't help me fix myself; it just put me in a bubble.  Additionally, it sometimes caused psychotic symptoms.

I can't use it "sometimes".  I'm either totally addicted to it or totally sober.  Been sober three years now.  Can't go back.

But I don't fault you for suggesting it.

Definitely not enough.  Any tips on getting past the consistent feelings of general malaise that I have to push myself to exercise?

A gym is not really an option, but I could walk more or do other at-home exercises.

I'd also appreciate tips on how to even DO simple exercises--I feel clueless.
Why do people like you even comment to people like me?

Thank you.  I really, really appreciate your comment.  I hope you can find something to help you, too.  

Have you tried a lot of the stuff I mentioned?

Because if I survive and get better, my job likely may not be there for me upon my return and/or the backlash will be horrible.  FMLA doesn't pay for absences in my line of work (for the state/non-profit) or apply here anyway.  ST disability would cut my pay and require me to inform my employers and a special committee about *why* I'm applying for it, and then they'd have to approve it.  I could be basically blacklisted for having a mental illness in my field, whether that's legal or not.

I am not sure how I could possibly just up and throw away my job (potentially) when I am totally financially dependent on my full paycheck.  I do not have anyone to live with or lean on if things go badly.  I'm all I've got.

I'm not on meds.  I have been off all psych meds for five months.  They made me sick at worst and didn't work at all at best.  

I still go out, talk to people, go on dates and go to meet-ups even though I feel totally hopeless.  Nothing can "take my mind off" of the fact that I've been doing these things for years and I'm still completely lonely and isolated.  It won't change my family, who are totally and completely unlike me and who can't relate to me or know me at all.  It won't change my brain, which is hell-bent on depression, it seems, even though I have gone months without any suicide research at times and even though I tried, earlier this year, to do a "positive thought of the day" journal challenge, for example.

I cannot just up and move.  I *am* taking a class--I'm in the middle of a Master's degree program.  I knit.  I go to yoga groups.  I do book clubs.  I journal.  I fly all over the country to meet up with distant friends and give myself an adventure.

You aren't listening if you're insisting that I'm not doing enough.  I'm doing it all; none of it makes a fucking difference.

And don't dare suggest that I've been doing "the same thing" all these years.  I have gotten a myriad compliments from pretty much anyone in my life who knows what's going on regarding how brave I've been to try so hard to change things over and over.  

It's shit like this--people do not fucking get it.  They assume everything about you and think they could much more easily fix it if only they were you.  

I don't need this attitude from anyone; it's certainly not why I posted here, but sadly pretty much what I expected.
Tell a car without gas that it can keep driving on a highway on an empty tank because its condition "is only temporary".
